summary_en: Orchestra Holdings to acquire Sharing Innovations via simplified share exchange, making it a wholly owned subsidiary effective 2026-11-30. Sharing Innovations stock to delist from TSE Growth Market 2026-11-26. Acquisition driven by need for integrated decision-making and resource utilization within DX business; Sharing Innovations facing headwinds including annual listing costs of ¥40–50M and reduced engineer staffing post-2024.
title_en: Notice of Share Exchange Agreement Execution (Simplified Share Exchange) for Complete Subsidiary Status of Sharing Innovations Inc. by Orchestra Holdings Inc.
translation_en_brief:
Orchestra Holdings and Sharing Innovations announced execution of a share exchange agreement on 2026-08-25 under which Orchestra Holdings will become the parent company and Sharing Innovations will become a wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction is structured as a simplified share exchange under the Companies Act (Article 796(2)), requiring shareholder approval from Sharing Innovations at an extraordinary general meeting scheduled 2026-10-26 but not from Orchestra Holdings. The effective date is planned for 2026-11-30, with Sharing Innovations' stock delisting from the TSE Growth Market on 2026-11-26 (final trading day 2026-11-25).

Orchestra Holdings stated the rationale as follows: the DX market environment is rapidly changing due to generative AI proliferation, rising customer demands, and intensified competition for IT talent. While Sharing Innovations—established in 2008 and now engaged in cloud integration, data analytics, AI services, and a native app divination business—is part of the Orchestra Holdings group, its listed status imposes governance constraints on intercompany transactions and resource sharing. Current annual listing costs are ¥40–50M. Sharing Innovations has faced declining engineer staffing (suspension of new graduate hiring since 2024) and compressed profitability after peak Salesforce implementation demand subsided around 2022.

Both boards determined that full subsidiary status will accelerate decision-making, enable integrated deployment of development and sales resources on large-scale projects, facilitate cross-selling via combined customer bases, and improve engineering quality and productivity through shared talent and technical expertise—thereby raising enterprise value for both entities and the wider Orchestra Holdings group.
